summary: This is a JUnit test class for the Thermostat, with one focused test per possible status in both regular and eco mode, plus a test for the display message. Each test creates a thermostat at a chosen temperature and checks that getStatus() reports the expected result.

lines.text: Brings in the @Test annotation from JUnit 5, which marks a method as a test the framework should run.
A static import lets you write assertEquals(...) directly instead of Assertions.assertEquals(...), keeping the tests short and readable.
Test classes conventionally take the name of the class under test with "Test" appended, so the pairing is obvious at a glance.
The method name states the expected behaviour as a sentence, so a failure report tells you what broke without your having to read the body.
Each test builds its own thermostat, so tests never share state and can run in any order. The false argument means eco mode is off.
assertEquals compares the expected value (first) with the actual value (second); the test passes only if they match exactly.
72 sits inside the comfortable band in regular mode, so no heating or cooling should be requested.
76 is above the regular-mode upper limit, which exercises the cooling branch.
Eco mode widens the acceptable range, so this test checks that a temperature which would be Idle in regular mode still triggers heating in eco mode.
Passing true switches eco mode on, shifting the thresholds the status logic uses.
66 falls in eco mode's wider comfort band, so the thermostat should stay idle and save energy.
79 pushes past even eco mode's raised cooling threshold, confirming cooling still kicks in eventually.
This last test covers the display method rather than the status itself, checking that the wording sent to the screen is built correctly.
Because printStatusToDisplay returns a String instead of printing, its full output can be asserted directly in a test.
